claim: Amazon Ads defines ACOS (advertising cost of sales) as a metric used to measure Amazon pay-per-click advertising campaigns.
evidence: Amazon advertising cost of sales (ACOS) is a metric used to measure Amazon pay-per-click (PPC) advertising campaigns.

claim: Amazon Ads gives the ACOS formula as ad spend divided by ad revenue, multiplied by 100.
evidence: ACOS = (ad spend ÷ ad revenue) x 100

claim: In Amazon Ads' example, $50 of ad spend that earns $100 gives an ACOS of 50%.
evidence: if you spent $50 on an ad campaign and earned $100 from it, your Amazon ACOS would be 50%.

claim: Amazon Ads describes ROAS as the inverse of ACOS, calculated by dividing ad revenue by ad spend.
evidence: Return on ad spend (ROAS) is the inverse of Amazon ACOS: it is calculated by dividing ad revenue by ad spend.

claim: In the same $50 spend / $100 revenue example, Amazon Ads says ROAS would be 2.
evidence: In the example above, the ROAS would be 2.

claim: Amazon Ads states there is no definitive number for a good ACOS.
evidence: There isn’t a definitive number for a good Amazon ACOS.

claim: Amazon Ads says a good ACOS depends on industry, company size and campaign frequency, among other variables.
evidence: It’s dependent on your industry, company size, and campaign frequency, among other variables.

claim: Amazon Ads says break-even ACOS is directly linked to profit margin.
evidence: Break-even ACOS is directly linked to your profit margin.

claim: Amazon Ads says that to maintain a profit, ACOS needs to be lower than profit margin.
evidence: In order to maintain a profit, your Amazon ACOS needs to be lower than your profit margin.

claim: Amazon Ads says each brand will have a different target ACOS, and the first step is achieving break-even ACOS and comparing it to profit margin.
evidence: Each brand is different and will have a different target ACOS.

claim: Amazon Ads defines CPC (cost per click) as a metric that determines how much advertisers pay for their ads, based on clicks.
publisher: Amazon Ads — Cost per click guide
evidence: CPC (cost per click) is a metric that determines how much advertisers pay for the ads they place on websites or social media

claim: Amazon Ads says the final CPC is usually determined by an auction, based on the adjusted bid plus additional factors.
publisher: Amazon Ads — Cost per click guide
evidence: The final CPC is usually determined by an auction and is based on your adjusted bid plus additional factors.

claim: Amazon Ads says the maximum cost per click is the highest amount an advertiser could be charged for a click, which includes the base bid plus any adjustments from settings such as dynamic bidding or cost controls.
publisher: Amazon Ads — Cost per click guide
evidence: which includes their base bid plus any adjustments from settings such as dynamic bidding or cost controls.

claim: Amazon Ads says that, generally, the more in-demand a keyword or the more visible the placement, the higher the advertising cost.

evidence: Generally, the more in-demand a keyword is or the more visible the placement, the higher the advertising costs.

claim: Amazon Ads describes average cost per click as the average amount spent on each click for an ad.

evidence: The average cost per click is easy: It’s the average amount spent on each click for an ad.

claim: Amazon Ads defines click-through rate (CTR) as the rate of the number of clicks an ad receives to another page.

evidence: The click-through rate (CTR) of an ad, landing page, or article is the rate of the number of clicks to another page

claim: Amazon Ads gives conversion rate as conversions divided by total audience, multiplied by 100.
evidence: Conversion rate = (conversions ÷ total audience) x 100
